## cli-reference

Regenerate the committed CLI documentation from the tools' own declarations.

`npm run cli-reference` — `scripts/ops/cli-reference.ts`

```
Regenerate the committed CLI documentation from the tools' own declarations.

When to use:
  Run this after changing any tool's defineCommand() block — its summary, flags, examples or
  subcommands. The generated files are committed, and `npm test` fails when they are stale, so
  this is the fix for that failure. Never hand-edit the generated files.

Writes <dir>/CLI_README.md (the full --help), docs/cli-reference.md (an index only) and
docs/cli-tools.json (the machine catalogue). Discovery is the registry in lib/cli/tiers.ts,
not a glob, and a file is statically checked for `export const cmd` / `defineCommand(` /
`import.meta.url` before it is imported — importing an unconverted tool would RUN it.

Usage:
  cli-reference [options]

  This command WRITES. It is dry by default: nothing changes without --apply.

Options:
  --check                    Write nothing; exit 1 if any generated file is stale or a tool failed to load

Common options:
  --format <string>          Output format (default: human on a terminal, json otherwise)  (one of: human, json)
  --quiet                    Suppress non-essential output on stderr
  --color                    Colourise human output (default: on a terminal)
  --help                     Show this help and exit
  --apply                    Actually write. Without it nothing is changed.
  --dry-run                  Report what would change and write nothing (the default)
  --yes                      Skip the confirmation prompt. Required with --apply off a terminal.

Output:
  --format human   aligned text — the default at a terminal
  --format json    JSON on stdout — the default when stdout is not a terminal
  Data goes to stdout; all diagnostics go to stderr.

External access:
  None. This command is pure — it reaches no database, API or credential.

Examples:
  npm run cli:reference
  npm run cli:reference -- --apply
  npm run cli:reference -- --check

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    generated files are stale (--check), or a listed tool could not be loaded
  2    usage error
  130  interrupted
```

## cli-conformance

Check that every operator CLI is registered and on the shared harness.

`npm run cli-conformance` — `scripts/ops/cli-conformance.ts`

```
Check that every operator CLI is registered and on the shared harness.

When to use:
  Run this after adding a CLI, or when `npm run check:cli` fails. It answers two questions the
  generated reference cannot: is anything claimed that does not exist, and is anything present
  that was never declared.

Reports MISSING (the manifest names a file that is gone), NOT_CONVERTED and
NO_ENTRYPOINT_GUARD (a tier A/B tool that is not on the harness) and UNTIERED (a CLI-shaped
file the manifest omits). The census currently walks scripts/ops only — see the 🛑 note in
lib/cli/census.ts before widening it.

Usage:
  cli-conformance [options]

  Read-only. This command changes nothing.

Options:
  --tier <string>            Only report findings for files in this tier  (one of: a, b, c, lib)

Common options:
  --format <string>          Output format (default: human on a terminal, json otherwise)  (one of: human, json)
  --quiet                    Suppress non-essential output on stderr
  --color                    Colourise human output (default: on a terminal)
  --help                     Show this help and exit

Output:
  --format human   aligned text — the default at a terminal
  --format json    JSON on stdout — the default when stdout is not a terminal
  Data goes to stdout; all diagnostics go to stderr.

External access:
  None. This command is pure — it reaches no database, API or credential.

Examples:
  npm run check:cli
  npm run check:cli -- --tier a

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    at least one finding
  2    usage error
  130  interrupted
```
